metadata.caption: Flow of proofs for welfare-like, revenue-like, positive tradeoff and negative tradeoff reward. For each, we give monotonicity results (for either allocation or reward), establish the form of the optimal mechanism (w.l.o.g.), and finally give an optimal rental mechanism. Although some intermediate results appear to be the same across different types, each result is proven separately and leverages characteristics specific to the reward.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1: Optimal are allocation monotone
nodes.statement:
For a welfare-like reward function:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a fixed-rate\xspace\ and strongly-allocation-monotone\xspace\ optimal SWAC\xspace.
        \item All truthful optimal SWACs\xspace\ are weakly-allocation-monotone\xspace. 
        \item If either the reward or the cost function are strictly increasing, all truthful SWACs\xspace\ are allocation-monotone\xspace.
        \item All truthful optimal SWACs\xspace\ are reward-monotone\xspace.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2: Optimal are reward monotone
nodes.statement: A truthful and optimal SWAC\xspace with respect to revenue-like reward is reward-monotone\xspace.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.6: Optimal are allocation monotone
nodes.statement:
Any finite-menu SWAC\xspace\ that is FM-optimal with respect to a positive or negative tradeoff reward
    is strongly-allocation-monotone\xspace.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.6, Lemma 5.7: Optimal are allocation monotone
nodes.statement:
Any finite-menu SWAC\xspace\ that is FM-optimal with respect to a positive or negative tradeoff reward
    is strongly-allocation-monotone\xspace.

For consumer surplus, 
    all truthful and optimal SWACs\xspace\ are allocation-monotone\xspace.

nodes.name: Corollary 5.4: Fixed-rate are w l o g
nodes.statement: For any optimal stagewise auction $\mathsf{A}$ with respect to a revenue-like reward, there exists a fixed-rate\xspace\ stagewise auction $\mathsf{A}'$ such that $\mathbb{E}\left[ \mathsf{A}' \right]=\mathbb{E}\left[ \mathsf{A} \right]$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.10: Fixed-rate are w l o g
Corollary 7.3, Lemma 5.11: Requires higher payment for first unit Cor Lem
nodes.statement:
For negative tradeoff reward, fixed-rate\xspace payment schedules are not w.l.o.g.

Let $\alloc:\mathcal{V}\rightarrow[n]$ be a monotone non-decreasing step-function, and let $\mathsf{A}$ be the matching threshold auction. It holds that:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathsf{A}$ is truthful.
        \item If the reward is a negative tradeoff reward, then 
        given another truthful auction $\mathsf{A}'$ with allocation rule $\alloc$, the expected rewards satisfy $\mathbb{E}\left[ \trew[\mathsf{A}]{v} \right]\geq\mathbb{E}\left[ \trew[\mathsf{A}']{v} \right]$.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 6.7: Find optimal threshold rental mechanism
nodes.statement: Algorithm~alg:consumer-surplus-auc is an FM-optimal and truthful negative tradeoff SWAC\xspace with over-time cost, for any horizon $n$ and distribution $\mathcal{D}$. For consumer surplus, it is globally optimal.
